name: Numeric Pain Rating Scale
description: Single-item measure of current pain intensity on an eleven-point scale.
instructions: Ask the patient to rate their pain on a scale from 0 to 10, where 0 is no pain and 10 is the worst pain imaginable. Record the current rating, and where useful the worst and best rating over the preceding week.
scoring_system: 0 to 10. Higher scores indicate greater pain intensity. A change of two points is commonly treated as clinically meaningful.
equipment_needed: None
contraindications: Not suitable where the patient cannot comprehend the scale. Consider an observational measure instead.

questions.question_text: On a scale from 0 to 10, where 0 is no pain and 10 is the worst pain imaginable, how would you rate your pain right now?

references: Hawker GA, Mian S, Kendzerska T, French M. Measures of adult pain. Arthritis Care Res. 2011;63(S11):S240-52.

rights.note: Non-proprietary and in universal clinical use. No rights-holder statement exists to confirm against.

name: Patient-Specific Functional Scale
description: Patient-nominated measure of functional limitation. The patient names the activities that matter to them and rates each one.
instructions: Ask the patient to name up to five activities they are unable to do, or have difficulty with, because of their problem. Record each activity in the patient's own words. Ask them to rate each activity from 0 to 10. Re-rate the same activities at review.
scoring_system: Each activity 0 (unable to perform) to 10 (able to perform at pre-injury level). Report individual activity scores and the mean. Higher is better.
equipment_needed: None

questions.question_text: Name an activity you are unable to do, or are having difficulty with, because of your problem.
Rate your ability to perform that activity today, where 0 is unable to perform and 10 is able to perform at your pre-injury level.

references: Stratford P, Gill C, Westaway M, Binkley J. Assessing disability and change on individual patients: a report of a patient specific measure. Physiother Can. 1995;47(4):258-63.

rights.note: Freely usable for clinical and research purposes without licence or fee.

name: Global Rating of Change
description: Single-item measure of the patient's own perception of overall change since the start of the episode.
instructions: Ask the patient to rate their overall change since the beginning of treatment on a bipolar scale.
scoring_system: Bipolar scale from -7 (a very great deal worse) through 0 (no change) to +7 (a very great deal better). Higher is better.
equipment_needed: None
conditions_indicated: Any episode of care requiring a global outcome

questions.question_text: Overall, how would you describe your condition now compared with when you first began treatment?

references: Kamper SJ, Maher CG, Mackay G. Global Rating of Change scales. J Man Manip Ther. 2009;17(3):163-70.

rights.holder: methodological construct; no single proprietary instrument
rights.note: A measurement approach rather than a copyrighted form. The item wording here is the platform's own and carries no licensing exposure.

name: Timed Up and Go
description: Timed measure of functional mobility and transfer ability, widely used as a falls-risk screen.
instructions: The patient sits in a standard armchair. On the command 'go' they rise, walk three metres at a comfortable and safe pace, turn, walk back and sit down. Time from the command to the moment they are seated again. One practice trial is permitted.
scoring_system: Time in seconds. Lower is better. Times of approximately fourteen seconds or more are commonly treated as indicating increased falls risk in community-dwelling older adults.
equipment_needed: Standard armchair, stopwatch, three-metre marked walkway
contraindications: Acute lower limb injury, unstable cardiovascular status, inability to stand safely with the usual aid
references: Podsiadlo D, Richardson S. The timed 'Up and Go': a test of basic functional mobility for frail elderly persons. J Am Geriatr Soc. 1991;39(2):142-8.

rights.note: No copyright asserted. Free for clinical and research use.

name: Functional Reach Test
description: Measure of standing balance and stability limits, expressed as maximal forward reach without stepping.
instructions: The patient stands with feet shoulder-width apart beside a wall-mounted ruler, shoulder flexed to ninety degrees with a closed fist. Record the starting knuckle position, then ask them to reach as far forward as possible without stepping or losing balance. Record the final position. The reach distance is the difference.
scoring_system: Distance in centimetres. Higher is better. A reach of less than fifteen centimetres is commonly treated as indicating increased falls risk.
equipment_needed: Wall-mounted ruler or measuring tape
contraindications: Unsafe standing balance without support, acute vertigo
references: Duncan PW, Weiner DK, Chandler J, Studenski S. Functional reach: a new clinical measure of balance. J Gerontol. 1990;45(6):M192-7.

rights.note: Non-proprietary. No rights-holder statement located, which is consistent with that status.

name: Six-Minute Walk Test
description: Sub-maximal measure of functional exercise capacity, expressed as the distance walked in six minutes.
instructions: Use a flat, straight corridor of known length with turnaround markers. Record resting heart rate, oxygen saturation and rating of perceived exertion. The patient walks as far as possible in six minutes at their own pace, resting if required without stopping the clock. Provide standardised encouragement only. Record post-test measures and the total distance.
scoring_system: Distance in metres. Higher is better. Interpret against published reference equations for age, sex, height and weight.
equipment_needed: Measured corridor, stopwatch, pulse oximeter, chair, cones
contraindications: Unstable angina or myocardial infarction within the preceding month. Relative contraindications include resting tachycardia and uncontrolled hypertension.
references: ATS Committee on Proficiency Standards for Clinical Pulmonary Function Laboratories. ATS statement: guidelines for the six-minute walk test. Am J Respir Crit Care Med. 2002;166(1):111-7.

rights.holder: test procedure non-proprietary; the American Thoracic Society statement is copyright
rights.note: The timed-walk procedure is free to implement. The American Thoracic Society guideline text is copyright and is cited here rather than reproduced.

name: Berg Balance Scale
description: Fourteen-item performance measure of static and dynamic balance.
instructions: Administer the fourteen standardised balance tasks in order, scoring each from 0 to 4 against the published criteria. Item wording and the scoring criteria must be imported from the custodial source rather than transcribed; see the rights note.
scoring_system: Fourteen items scored 0 to 4, summed to a maximum of 56. Higher is better.
equipment_needed: Chair with armrests, chair without armrests, stopwatch, ruler, step or stool
contraindications: Inability to stand safely even with supervision
references: Berg K, Wood-Dauphinee S, Williams JI, Gayton D. Measuring balance in the elderly: preliminary development of an instrument. Physiother Can. 1989;41(6):304-11.

rights.note: Public domain, so no licence is required. Item wording is nevertheless withheld from this build because it must be imported verbatim from an authoritative published source rather than transcribed from recollection. Public domain is a licensing position, not a warrant for approximate item text in a clinical record.
rights.licenceRoute: Import verbatim item text and scoring criteria from the original publication before enabling the scored runner.

name: Roland-Morris Disability Questionnaire
description: Twenty-four item measure of disability arising from low back pain.
instructions: Record the total score. Item wording must be imported verbatim from the custodial source at rmdq.org before the scored runner is enabled; see the rights note.
scoring_system: Twenty-four yes or no items, summed 0 to 24. Higher scores indicate greater disability. Commonly preferred over the Oswestry Disability Index at lower levels of disability.
equipment_needed: None
references: Roland M, Morris R. A study of the natural history of back pain. Spine. 1983;8(2):141-4.

rights.note: The custodial site confirms the questionnaire and its translations are free of permission requirements and free of charge. Item wording is withheld from this build only because it must be imported verbatim from that source rather than transcribed.
rights.licenceRoute: Download the current item text from rmdq.org and import it verbatim, then enable the scored runner.

name: Oswestry Disability Index
description: Ten-section measure of disability arising from low back pain. Score capture only in this build.
instructions: This platform does not reproduce the questionnaire. Administer the instrument from your own licensed copy and record the resulting percentage here.
scoring_system: Ten sections scored 0 to 5, summed and expressed as a percentage from 0 to 100. Higher scores indicate greater disability.
equipment_needed: Your own licensed copy of the instrument
references: Fairbank JCT, Pynsent PB. The Oswestry Disability Index. Spine. 2000;25(22):2940-53.

rights.holder: Jeremy Fairbank (1980); licensed via Mapi Research Trust
rights.note: Free for unfunded academic research and individual clinical practice. A licence fee applies to funded academic, commercial and health-organisation use, which includes reproduction inside a commercial platform.
rights.licenceRoute: Apply to Mapi Research Trust for a commercial licence before enabling the scored runner.

name: Neck Disability Index
description: Ten-section measure of disability arising from neck pain. Score capture only in this build.
instructions: This platform does not reproduce the questionnaire. Administer the instrument from your own permitted copy and record the resulting score here.
scoring_system: Ten sections scored 0 to 5, summed to 50 or expressed as a percentage. Higher scores indicate greater disability.
equipment_needed: Your own permitted copy of the instrument
references: Vernon H, Mior S. The Neck Disability Index: a study of reliability and validity. J Manipulative Physiol Ther. 1991;14(7):409-15.

rights.note: Reproductions carry an authors' permission notice and no centralised free-licensing route was identified, so permission is treated as required. Date attribution is unreconciled between sources.
rights.licenceRoute: Seek the authors' written permission before enabling the scored runner.

name: QuickDASH
description: Eleven-item measure of upper limb disability and symptoms. Score capture only in this build.
instructions: This platform does not reproduce the questionnaire. Administer the instrument from your own licensed copy and record the resulting score here.
scoring_system: Eleven items, transformed to a score from 0 (no disability) to 100 (most severe disability).
equipment_needed: Your own licensed copy of the instrument
references: Beaton DE, Wright JG, Katz JN. Development of the QuickDASH. J Bone Joint Surg Am. 2005;87(5):1038-46.

rights.holder: Institute for Work and Health, Toronto
rights.note: A hard commercial gate. Free for a clinician treating individual patients and for non-commercial research, but incorporation into commercial software is a licensed category requiring an approved user profile, a signed licence and a fee before any use.
rights.licenceRoute: Execute an Institute for Work and Health commercial software licence before enabling the scored runner.

name: Knee injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score
description: Knee-specific measure across five subscales. Score capture only in this build.
instructions: This platform does not reproduce the questionnaire. Administer the instrument from your own licensed copy and record the subscale scores here.
scoring_system: Five subscales, each transformed to 0 (extreme problems) to 100 (no problems).
equipment_needed: Your own licensed copy of the instrument
references: Roos EM, Roos HP, Lohmander LS, Ekdahl C, Beynnon BD. Knee Injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score (KOOS). J Orthop Sports Phys Ther. 1998;28(2):88-96.

rights.holder: Professor Ewa Roos; distribution via Mapi Research Trust since May 2023
rights.note: A licence or registration is required of every user, including free-tier users. A fee applies to health organisations and commercial users.
rights.licenceRoute: Register and licence through Mapi Research Trust before enabling the scored runner.

name: Hip disability and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score
description: Hip-specific measure across five subscales. Score capture only in this build.
instructions: This platform does not reproduce the questionnaire. Administer the instrument from your own licensed copy and record the subscale scores here.
scoring_system: Five subscales, each transformed to 0 (extreme problems) to 100 (no problems).
equipment_needed: Your own licensed copy of the instrument
references: Nilsdotter AK, Lohmander LS, Klassbo M, Roos EM. Hip disability and osteoarthritis outcome score (HOOS). BMC Musculoskelet Disord. 2003;4:10.

rights.holder: Professor Ewa Roos; distribution via Mapi Research Trust
rights.note: Registration is required regardless of fee status. Sources conflict on the fee liability for ordinary clinical practice; commercial embedding is treated as fee-bearing until confirmed with the distributor.
rights.licenceRoute: Register and licence through Mapi Research Trust before enabling the scored runner.

name: Lower Extremity Functional Scale
description: Twenty-item measure of lower limb functional limitation. Score capture only in this build.
instructions: This platform does not reproduce the questionnaire. Administer the instrument from your own permitted copy and record the resulting score here.
scoring_system: Twenty items scored 0 to 4, summed to a maximum of 80. Higher is better.
equipment_needed: Your own permitted copy of the instrument
references: Binkley JM, Stratford PW, Lott SA, Riddle DL. The Lower Extremity Functional Scale (LEFS). Phys Ther. 1999;79(4):371-83.

rights.holder: Binkley, Stratford, Lott and Riddle (1999); reprinted with American Physical Therapy Association permission
rights.note: Commonly described informally as free, but reprints carry a permission notice and the instrument appears in a commercial licensing catalogue. Withheld pending confirmation.
rights.licenceRoute: Confirm the current position with Mapi Research Trust or the American Physical Therapy Association.

name: STarT Back Screening Tool
description: Nine-item prognostic screening tool stratifying low back pain into low, medium and high risk of a poor outcome. Score capture only in this build.
instructions: This platform does not reproduce the questionnaire. Administer the instrument from your own registered copy and record the total and psychosocial subscale scores here.
scoring_system: Nine items yielding a total score and a psychosocial subscale score, stratifying into low, medium or high risk.
equipment_needed: Your own registered copy of the instrument
conditions_indicated: Low back pain in primary care
references: Hill JC, Dunn KM, Lewis M, et al. A primary care back pain screening tool. Arthritis Rheum. 2008;59(5):632-41.

rights.note: Free to public-sector bodies and non-commercial research groups subject to mandatory registration with Keele University. A commercial platform requires a case-by-case licence agreement.
rights.licenceRoute: Register with Keele University and negotiate a commercial licence before enabling the scored runner.

name: Orebro Musculoskeletal Pain Screening Questionnaire
description: Screening questionnaire for psychosocial risk of chronicity and work disability in musculoskeletal pain. Score capture only in this build.
instructions: This platform does not reproduce the questionnaire. Administer the instrument from your own permitted copy and record the resulting score here.
scoring_system: Varies by version. Long and short forms are summed and interpreted against published cut-points.
equipment_needed: Your own permitted copy of the instrument
references: Linton SJ, Boersma K. Early identification of patients at risk of developing a persistent back problem. Clin J Pain. 2003;19(2):80-6.

rights.holder: Linton (1997); short form Linton and Boersma (2003)
rights.note: Reproduced by Australian compensation schemes without an evident fee gate, which indicates tolerated scheme use rather than a general licence.
rights.licenceRoute: Seek the developer's confirmation of permitted commercial use.

name: Tampa Scale for Kinesiophobia
description: Measure of fear of movement and re-injury. Score capture only in this build.
instructions: This platform does not reproduce the questionnaire. Administer the instrument from your own permitted copy and record the resulting score here.
scoring_system: The seventeen-item version sums to a range of 17 to 68; the eleven-item version to 11 to 44. Higher scores indicate greater kinesiophobia.
equipment_needed: Your own permitted copy of the instrument
references: Woby SR, Roach NK, Urmston M, Watson PJ. Psychometric properties of the TSK-11. Pain. 2005;117(1-2):137-44.

rights.note: No centralised licensing portal was identified. Treated as requiring the rights holder's permission.
rights.licenceRoute: Establish the current rights position before enabling the scored runner.

name: Pain Catastrophising Scale
description: Thirteen-item measure of catastrophic thinking about pain. Score capture only in this build.
instructions: This platform does not reproduce the questionnaire. Administer the instrument from your own licensed copy and record the resulting score here.
scoring_system: Thirteen items scored 0 to 4, summed 0 to 52. Higher scores indicate greater catastrophising.
equipment_needed: Your own licensed copy of the instrument
references: Sullivan MJL, Bishop SR, Pivik J. The Pain Catastrophizing Scale: development and validation. Psychol Assess. 1995;7(4):524-32.

rights.holder: Michael J. L. Sullivan; licensed via Mapi Research Trust
rights.note: Permission or licence is required notwithstanding the instrument's ubiquity in the literature.
rights.licenceRoute: Licence through Mapi Research Trust before enabling the scored runner.

name: Victorian Institute of Sport Assessment - Achilles
description: Eight-item measure of Achilles tendinopathy severity. Score capture only in this build.
instructions: This platform does not reproduce the questionnaire. Administer the instrument from your own copy and record the resulting score here.
scoring_system: Eight items summed to a maximum of 100. A score of 100 indicates an asymptomatic, fully functional tendon.
equipment_needed: Your own copy of the instrument
references: Robinson JM, Cook JL, Purdam C, et al. The VISA-A questionnaire. Br J Sports Med. 2001;35(5):335-41.

rights.note: Widespread reproduction without an evident fee suggests free clinical use with attribution, but that is an inference rather than a rights-holder statement. This instrument also appears in the exercise-physiology catalogue, so the determination bears on the existing live product as well.
rights.licenceRoute: Establish the rights position with the originating institution.

name: Victorian Institute of Sport Assessment - Patellar
description: Eight-item measure of patellar tendinopathy severity. Score capture only in this build.
instructions: This platform does not reproduce the questionnaire. Administer the instrument from your own copy and record the resulting score here.
scoring_system: Eight items summed to a maximum of 100. A score of 100 indicates an asymptomatic, fully functional tendon.
equipment_needed: Your own copy of the instrument
references: Visentini PJ, Khan KM, Cook JL, et al. The VISA score. J Sci Med Sport. 1998;1(1):22-8.

rights.note: Same authorship lineage and same unresolved rights position as the Achilles version.
rights.licenceRoute: Establish the rights position with the originating institution.

name: Active Range of Motion
description: Goniometric measurement of active joint range, recorded per movement and compared bilaterally.
instructions: Position the patient according to the standard technique for the joint under examination. Align the goniometer to the recognised bony landmarks. Ask the patient to move actively through the available range and record the angle at the end of range, together with the pain response.
scoring_system: Degrees, recorded per movement and side. Interpret against the contralateral side and published normal ranges.
equipment_needed: Goniometer or inclinometer
contraindications: Acute fracture, recent surgery where movement is restricted by protocol, joint instability
conditions_indicated: Any musculoskeletal presentation involving restricted movement

rights.note: A measurement technique rather than a proprietary instrument.

name: Manual Muscle Testing - Oxford Scale
description: Graded assessment of muscle strength using the Oxford zero-to-five scale, recorded per muscle group and side.
instructions: Position the patient to isolate the muscle group. Apply resistance appropriate to the grade being tested and record the highest grade achieved without substitution.
scoring_system: 0 no contraction; 1 flicker of contraction; 2 active movement with gravity eliminated; 3 active movement against gravity; 4 active movement against gravity and some resistance; 5 normal power.
equipment_needed: None, or a hand-held dynamometer where available
contraindications: Acute fracture, recent tendon repair, unstable joint, pain that precludes resisted testing

rights.note: A long-established clinical grading scale in general use.

name: Neurological Screening Examination
description: Structured screen of myotomes, dermatomes and deep tendon reflexes for the upper or lower limb.
instructions: Test each myotome against resistance, each dermatome for light touch and sharp or blunt discrimination, and the relevant deep tendon reflexes. Record findings by level and by side, and note any asymmetry.
scoring_system: Recorded per level and side as normal, reduced or absent. Reflexes graded 0 to 4 on the standard scale.
equipment_needed: Tendon hammer, cotton wool, neurotip

rights.note: A standard clinical examination sequence rather than a proprietary instrument.
